cells.tense: The thing you made has settled into its own shape, and you can see what it returns to you.
cells.ask: Say out loud what return you want from the finished thing, ask once for it, and leave the answer alone.
cells.core: You finished something and it holds without you holding it. The pride isn't loud. It sits under the next move like a floor. What's working is that you can see the whole exchange — what you put in, what comes back — and you're not scrambling to tip it your way. When it's right, you know it before anyone tells you, and you trust that knowing instead of second-guessing whether you got enough. That steadiness is the thing to lean on here. Name what the work owes you, ask for it in one clean sentence, and let the answer arrive or not without you managing it. The work already stands on its own. Let the share land the same way, collected quietly and carried forward.
cells.sheetLine: You made it, it holds, and you know what it owes you.

cells.tense: You are already out past the finished thing, bracing for how the next settlement will go.
cells.ask: Show one person the finished work before you fix it, then don't touch it for a day after they see it.
cells.core: The push leans forward past what's done. Something you brought to stand is still sitting there, and you're already guarding it against a version of events that hasn't happened — who might take from it, what the next exchange will cost you. The bracing is the toll. You can't take in what came back if you're already renegotiating it in your head. Done right, the finished thing just sits there and you collect what it gave you, no defense needed. Let one person look at it as it is. Let the gap between what you made and what you want from it stay open a day without you rushing to fill it.

cells.tense: You built the thing and then stepped away from the door where you'd have to look at it.
cells.ask: Pick one finished piece and write three lines on what it returned to you — money, time, or ease — without judging if it's enough.
cells.core: You stopped presenting what you made. The accounting hasn't been closed, and you quit putting it on the table. The thing is still there, finished, whether you turn toward it or not. What's gone is the ability to see the shape of what you brought to stand, from this side of it. You don't have to feel proud to name it. Just turn toward one finished piece and let it be what it is — the size of it, what it gave, what it asked. One honest look tells you what you're doing to the next move by not counting this one. The record already holds it. Reading it back is the way forward.

cells.tense: You are already keeping the ledger of what's fair, and you call it just getting through the day.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did today out of fairness, as your own choice, not what anyone expected.
cells.core: You already see what's out of proportion around you, and you adjust it without ceremony. The correction is small, the sentence is quick, and nobody notices — least of all you. That steady leveling is you shaping what happens, though it goes unclaimed. It runs so quietly that when the question of return comes up, you treat it like something happening to you instead of something you set. One adjustment you made today was yours to make. Put your own word on it before it disappears into the ordinary pile. That is the return you have been owed — partly the act itself, partly your own account of it, kept where you can see it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already leveling things. Start claiming you do it.

attempts.check: The record says the Achievement capacity has produced lasting form, and the seat is driven by one question: does it balance? I read that as a person who has built something and now checks it against fair return. The reader could object that their work is still underway, not something standing done, in which case the ask still holds — they can still say what return they want instead of only making more product. The sentence that flatters me more than them reads their stubbornness as dignity without naming anything I can see.
